author: independent Spring Boot 4 / Java 25 / Python / FastAPI SME critic (Claude subagent, not an item author; Final Assessment coding challenges review 2026-11-19, runs on copies; transcribed from critics/coding-challenges-sme)

findings.claim: [all four (cross-cutting)] The 70% per-question pass mark sits on coarse check counts, so many author-designated WRONG solutions still PASS the graded question. The checks discriminate at check level, but pass/fail does not. Python-2: 11 of 19 wrong variants pass, including wrong-01 (leaks reason + customer_email, 8/9), wrong-16 unscoped refunded total and wrong-17 refuses only 'authorized' (the two loop-0 SME HIGH false passes, which HANDOFF calls 'closed', both 8/9). My V3 (PII leak + timeout mapped to 502, two defects) scores 7/9 = pass. Python-1: 6 of 16 wrong pass (e.g. wrong-02 raw['txn_id'] KeyError 5/7, wrong-06 loops twice 5/7). Spring-10: 3 of 8 pass (N2, N5, N6) plus my X1 and X3. Spring-20 is the opposite: every recorded score is 0, 2, 4 or 6 of 6, so 70% means 6/6. Critic evidence: Recomputed from _private-reference/python-{1,2}/variants/expect.json; I re-ran both matrices with run-py.sh (0 mismatches). New variants: work/variants/p2/V2-leak-pii 8/9, V3-leak-pii-and-timeout-502 7/9. Spring matrices in */README.md 'Scoring at 70%'.
findings.recommendation: Owner decision, made once for all four. Recommended: name 1-2 gate checks per question that must pass (P2: check1 response fields plus check6/7 business rules; P1: check5/6; S10: check4), or weight checks by objective. Otherwise accept partial credit explicitly, and stop calling a false pass 'closed' when it still passes the question.

findings.claim: [python-1 (10 min)] The sort check is nondeterministic for a common wrong answer. Every multi-field case has exactly 2 fields, so 'fields': list({...}) (a set, not sorted) passes or fails depending on string hash order. The same submission scores anywhere from 4/7 to 7/7 between runs and can flip the pass/fail result: green locally, red at grading, or the reverse. Critic evidence: work/variants/p1/Z1-unsorted-set. Scores by PYTHONHASHSEED: 0 gives 7/7, 1 gives 5/7, 2 gives 6/7, 3 gives 4/7 (fail), 4 gives 7/7, 5 gives 7/7.
findings.recommendation: Make check4 use a record that fails 4 or more fields whose sorted order differs from declaration order (e.g. status/merchant/cardholder as non-str, plus amount and currency). A random order then passes about 1/24 of the time or less. Also add one 3+ field case to check2 or check6. Do not rely on PYTHONHASHSEED in grade.yml, because local runs would still differ.

findings.claim: [all four (cross-cutting)] The graded repos ship the oracle in learner-writable paths (tests/, starter/pom.xml with testSourceDirectory ../tests). Nothing in grade.yml restores the authoritative tests or pom before running. A learner can edit test_main.py or ToolLookupTest.java, or add <skipTests> to the pom, and the Spring run then exits 0 with no reports. The READMEs only ask learners to leave these files alone. Critic evidence: grade.yml runs `mvn -q -B -o -f starter/pom.xml test` or `python -m pytest -q ...` against whatever is in the learner repo. Python-2's HANDOFF already notes that the public tests can be special-cased.
findings.recommendation: Confirm that Exa overwrites tests/ and starter/pom.xml (and Python conftest/pytest config) from the authoritative copy at grade time, or add a setup step that does. Treat a missing or empty surefire report as 0.

findings.claim: [python-1, python-2, spring-10min] The learner-facing labels are stale or inconsistent. The Python titles say 'Python checkpoint question (basic/intermediate)' while the Spring titles say 'Spring final assessment'. Python-2's title never says FastAPI. The Spring-10 test Javadoc says 'Spring checkpoint question I'. Timing wording also differs: P1 and S10 say 'including reading', P2 says '20 minutes of coding'. Python version guidance differs too: P1 says exactly 3.12, P2 says '3.12 or later', and grade.yml says 3.12. Both references pass on 3.14.6 with the pins, so this is wording only. Critic evidence: grep 'checkpoint' over repo/ trees. venv314 run: p1 reference 7/7, p2 reference 9/9.
findings.recommendation: Retitle all four 'Final assessment, coding question N (Python | Python/FastAPI | Spring)'. Use one timing sentence and one Python version statement.
